newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat export warning may cool Iraqi tender.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat export warning may cool Iraqi tender.

text.p: Warnings that the European Union may curb wheat sales will make exporters less aggressive in competing to sell grain to Iraq at a tender on Tuesday, grain traders said on Monday.
Grain companies have been jockeying to sell wheat to Iraq as Baghdad restores oil exports to pay for humanitarian relief.
But traders said the warning on Friday by EU agriculture director Guy Legras may encourage traders to be less aggressive in undercutting each other with low-priced wheat.
An EU export slowdown would usually prop up world prices.
"Exporters may be less aggressive (pricewise)," one French operator said.
Iraq launched a tender last week to import 100,000 tonnes of French wheat during January and February.
Traders have until Tuesday to submit their offers. Iraq has said it will take a decision on the tender by December 19.
Legras said on Friday that the EU might "turn the screw on exports" after authorising sales of more than one million tonnes of wheat in the previous two weeks.
He said this might happen at the next opportunity when the EU holds its weekly auction -- also on December 19.
Legras reiterated the warning on Monday.
Traders said they would be cautious about their offers to Iraq, which must be sent in before the next EU export tender.
But exporters who already have a comfortable number of export licences may be bolder than others, they said.
"It will depend on whether they hold long or short positions," one operator said.
Exporters said January shipment for the wheat may be hard to secure as it will take time to get the whole oil-for-food pact going.

Iraq is buying wheat under a UN-approved scheme to raise $2 billion over six months by selling crude oil for the first time since sanctions were imposed in August 1990. About half the $2 billion will be available for purchases of food and medicine under strict UN monitoring. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
